generation: Nine generations, 1996 to today. A game's generation is when it was released, not where it is set: HeartGold/SoulSilver are a gen IV remake set in the gen II region.
version-group: One game release, usually a pair of versions. 32 groups. order (1 to 32) is a global release timeline. The API doesn't say which groups are remakes, DLC or spin-offs, and a group can cover two regions (HeartGold/SoulSilver: Johto and Kanto).
version: 53 versions. Encounters and wild held items differ by version; learnsets and machines only by version group.
pokedex: 35 dexes: national plus regional, often several per game. A species has a different number in each (Pikachu #25 national, #74 Paldea).
type: 18 battle types (Dark and Steel from gen II, Fairy from gen VI) plus Stellar (Tera only), unknown (???) and shadow, which no Pokémon has as its own type. move_damage_class is the class every move of this type had before the gen IV physical/special split. past_damage_relations holds the gen I and gen V charts.
stat: Includes special, which only existed in gen I and only appears in pokemon.past_stats.
ability: Abilities start in gen III, hidden abilities in gen V.
move: Values changed between games: 198 recorded changes, 83 in X/Y. past_values lists only the changed fields, and they are the values from before the listed version group (Bite: normal, gold-silver; Bite was Normal in Red/Blue). Before gen IV a move's physical/special class came from its type.
machine: Which move a TM/HM/TR teaches depends on the game: TM26 is Earthquake in 20 version groups, then four other moves. 2,142 TMs, 130 HMs, 100 TRs.
pokemon-species: 1,025 species: 151, 100, 135, 107, 156, 72, 88, 96, 120 per generation. 71 legendary, 23 mythical, 19 baby.
pokemon: 1,351 battle varieties: 1,025 defaults plus 97 megas, 59 regional forms, 34 Gigantamax, 12 totems and other alternates. past_types replaces the whole typing; past_stats and past_abilities list only what changed; all three are valid up to and including their generation. One move can appear at several levels in one game (Smeargle's Sketch). Level 0 on a level-up move means "learnt on evolving" (gen VII+).
pokemon-form: 1,579 forms. Cosmetic forms (Unown letters, Vivillon patterns) exist only here; battle-relevant variants are separate pokemon. version_group is when the form first appeared: Alolan Raichu arrives in Sun/Moon.
evolution-chain: 540 chains, 676 rules. Chains are per species; region, required_pokemon_form and evolved_pokemon_form tell regional evolutions apart (Pikachu to Alolan Raichu only in Alola). One step can have several rules, one per game that changed it.
evolution-trigger: 18 triggers, from level-up and trade to spin, three-critical-hits and gimmighoul-coins.
location-area: 117,127 encounters. chance is a slot percentage in classic games, a relative weight for Let's Go and Sword/Shield overworld spawns, and always 100 for gifts and statics. No encounter data after Sword/Shield.
encounter-method: 66 methods: walking, surfing, three rods, headbutt, hordes, SOS, overworld wanderers, Max Raids, gifts, static encounters.
encounter-condition: 30 condition types: time, season, weather, swarm, Poké Radar, GBA cartridge in slot 2, radio, story progress and more.
item: 2,223 items. Held items started in gen II. TMs were single-use until gen V; HMs were removed in gen VII; TRs existed only in gen VIII.
region: Regions are modelled on real places: Kanto/Johto/Hoenn/Sinnoh on Japan, Unova on New York, Kalos on France, Alola on Hawaii, Galar on the UK, Paldea on Iberia. Hisui is ancient Sinnoh; Orre is the Colosseum/XD region.
